pr_title: Fix crash applying a filter repeated times quickly
pr_body:
This PR fixes two problems:
- First it fixes #4963 by introducing a new flag to the UI's ButtonBase click to prevent calling an onClick() handler inside of a previously called onClick() handler. There is a comment describing a situation where this can happen, which is the one happening in the resolved issue.

- Second, once fixed the above, there was a chance that the FilterPreview::onDelayedStartPreview() be called after a FilterPreview::stop() call, because the m_restarPreviewTimer was not being stopped when the preview was being stopped.

comments: I've been trying to reproduce this exact issue without luck. BUT, I've found out that by setting a negative alpha value and pressing the Apply button as fast as possible can generate crashes in random places of the code...so maybe this is an instance of doing that. I hope that fixing this be a matter of just synchronizing a bit some threads...will investigate.

Put some traces and using some atomic ints I've been able to confirm that when pressing the Apply button quickly, sometimes  the FilterWindow::onApply click handler is getting called before a previous FilterWindow::onApply finishes, which also creates more than one background thread to apply the filter. I'm still not sure why is this happening, I'm looking into it.

I was wrong, it wasn't creating more than one background thread. It was actually calling the FilterWindow::onApply from inside a previously FilterWindow::onApply call. This happens because the first onApply is called from the FilterWindow's event loop, and the other from the Alert window's event loop, because of how the system events are queued when pressing very quickly the FilterWindow's apply button. I'm about to push a PR.

I'm marking this as closed since the issue is very hard to reproduce. And there is a big chance that there is another thing that is causing the issue because in my testing one time the error was raised by pressing the Apply button as regular when the progress bar was close to 100%.

review_comments: Probably we can move the `m_behaviorType` field as the first field in this class, leaving all bool flags together (m_pressedStatus/m_clicking/m_handleSelect). This might reduce the class size, e.g. https://godbolt.org/z/rn9GfGT7a (try moving the `WidgetType` field of the `A` struct as the first field).
